run_note: Heads up: today's update only covers 14 of the usual 15 holdings. Thermo Fisher Scientific wasn't scored because of a technical problem on our side — nothing to do with the company itself.

LHX.sentence: L3Harris is down by about a third from its high, which is a lot given that it's the smallest of the big five defense contractors and defense budgets are still growing steadily — nothing about the business has really soured.

ASML.sentence: ASML bounced about 9% and is well off its peak, which is unusual for a company that's the only maker in the world of a certain essential chipmaking machine — demand for advanced chips keeps growing underneath the dip.

LIN.sentence: Linde is quietly doing its job — when markets get nervous, investors lean toward steady businesses like this industrial-gas supplier that sells oxygen and nitrogen on long contracts and nudges prices up a little each year.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft has pulled back a bit and looks a little tired, but the business is boring in the best way — the Azure cloud and AI story just keeps grinding along without drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher Scientific didn't get scored in today's run because of a technical problem on our side — nothing happened to the company itself. It should be back in tomorrow's update.

CVX.sentence: Chevron slipped a touch, and it's worth remembering its profits are swollen right now because Middle East tensions have pushed oil far above normal — that's the oil price, not the company getting better, and at the ordinary oil price it plans around it's not the bargain it might look like.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow jumped almost 5% but is still down sharply from its high, which is rare for a company like this — big companies and government agencies keep signing on for its workflow and AI-assistant tools under long, sticky contracts.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore fell about 3% even as copper surged — an odd split, since this is a miner that should benefit from rising copper, so the stock has lagged what the metal is actually doing.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta rose about 4%, and the price it gets per ton of crushed stone is still creeping up — that quiet pricing power is the real engine here, whatever the headline numbers look like.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA is flat today, but the Mexican peso is weakening, and since most of its sales are in pesos, that quietly chips away at the dollars this Latin American Coke bottler brings home.

UBER.sentence: Uber was roughly flat, and the thing that matters most — people booking more and more rides and food orders — is still growing nicely, even as self-driving-car companies decide whether to run on its app or go it alone.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk is calm this week; the stock is priced below what it would cost to replace its fleet of ships, which has historically been a decent long-term entry point for this container-shipping bellwether.

MA.sentence: Mastercard ticked up, and people keep tapping their cards more than ever — this is the business where it collects a tiny toll on each transaction, millions of times a day around the world.

ISRG.sentence: The da Vinci surgical-robot company rose about 4% and is trading at its deepest discount against its own recent history while sitting a third below its high — hospitals keep doing more operations with its machines, and every surgery means more disposable supplies sold.

NVDA.sentence: Nvidia surged sharply today, but the real question hanging over it is whether its handful of giant customers can keep paying — two of the four biggest are now spending more on computing gear than their businesses bring in and borrowing the rest, and that's about their wallets, not Nvidia's product.
